lines: ہزاروں خواہشیں ایسی کہ ہر خواہش پہ دم نکلے
بہت نکلے مرے ارمان لیکن پھر بھی کم نکلے
roman: Hazaaron khwahishen aisi ke har khwahish pe dam nikle
Bahut nikle mere armaan lekin phir bhi kam nikle
meaningEn: I have thousands of desires, each one worth dying for. Many of my wishes came true, and still it feels like too few.
whyItLands: Ghalib uses the same verb, nikle, in both lines. First it is breath leaving the body for a single wish; then it is wishes coming true. Longing and fulfilment share one word, and neither is ever enough.

lines: دل ناداں تجھے ہوا کیا ہے
آخر اس درد کی دوا کیا ہے
roman: Aakhir is dard ki dawa kya hai
meaningEn: My foolish heart, what has happened to you? What, after all, is the cure for this pain?
whyItLands: Ghalib speaks to his own heart as if it were a worried friend, which turns a private ache into something anyone can say out loud.

meaningEn: No hope ever comes true. No way forward can be seen.
whyItLands: Soorat means both a way out and a face, so the second line can also mean that no beloved face appears. Despair and loneliness share the line.

glossary.meaning: in bar aana: to be fulfilled
a way, a possibility; also a face

lines: تمہارے خط میں نیا اک سلام کس کا تھا
نہ تھا رقیب تو آخر وہ نام کس کا تھا
roman: Tumhare khat mein naya ik salaam kis ka tha
Na tha raqeeb to aakhir woh naam kis ka tha
meaningEn: Your letter carried a new greeting from someone. If it wasn't a rival, then whose name was that?
whyItLands: Playful jealousy. One extra greeting at the end of a letter is enough to start an investigation.

lines: لگتا نہیں ہے دل مرا اجڑے دیار میں
کس کی بنی ہے عالم ناپائیدار میں
roman: Lagta nahin hai dil mera ujre dayaar mein
Kis ki bani hai aalam-e-napaedaar mein
meaningEn: My heart can't settle in this ruined land. Who has ever made a lasting home in a world that doesn't last?
whyItLands: Read as the voice of the last Mughal emperor in exile, it is about losing a city and a world. Read on its own, it fits anyone far from a place they loved.
attributionNote: Widely attributed to Bahadur Shah Zafar, but some scholars question whether he wrote this ghazal.
